Manuel Academy RFL G3 Unit 1 — personal and shared space care

objective: I can check a space for a trip, poison, shock, fire, or choke risk. I will point without touching, name the risk or say “I am not sure,” and ask a guardian to handle anything unsafe.
scenario: A lamp cord stretches across the middle of a pictured walking path. The lamp is switched off.
safetyNotes: The learner points out and describes each hazard but does not pick up, move, or open any cleaning product, medicine, or sharp item themselves; the trusted adult handles those.
If a hazard involves electricity, heat, or a chemical container, the adult resolves it while the learner watches and describes what was fixed.
If the learner is unsure whether something counts as a hazard, the correct move is to point it out and ask, and asking counts as success.

simulationAlternative.description: If a real walkthrough of two spaces is not possible, the learner instead looks at four printed or hand-drawn pictures of rooms containing planted hazards, circles each unsafe item, and writes the specific reason it is unsafe.

prompts.text: Which move—spot, stop, name, or ask—helped you make a careful decision? Explain using an invented scene or only the risk word. Do not describe a private household item or room.

remediation: Contrast two embedded pictures: a strap across a path can cause a trip; a closed book flat on a shelf does not block a path. “Messy” is not a risk word. Name how harm could happen. Coach card: A toy bin is beside the path, but one long strap reaches into the path. Point to the condition and name the risk or say unsure. Confirm only observable moves: risk mechanism named, no-touch boundary used, and adult handoff stated. If a live-task safety error occurred, stop the live task and continue in simulation. Fresh card: A dry, unbroken cord runs along the wall and does not cross the path. Decide “risk,” “safe in this picture,” or “unsure,” and give one reason. Exit: On both fresh cards, the learner gives a risk-based reason and keeps the point-without-touching/ask boundary. Resume with the next unfinished independent scene. A Home Check resumes only when the guardian says it is safe; otherwise finish the equal-credit Scene Check.
extension: Have the learner and adult repeat the hazard walk in a third space that specifically differs from the first two, such as a garage or basement, using the same five-word target list.

resources.title: Five risk words and safe-or-unsure cues
resources.purpose: Used by the model, guided attempt, both independent routes, and retry.
content: Trip: Could this make someone fall?
Poison: Is this an unknown cleaner, medicine, or chemical?
Shock: Is a cord, plug, or electrical item damaged or wet?
Fire: Is heat, flame, or a hot item close to something that can burn?
Choke: Could a very small object be reached by a young child?
Safe or unsure: If you cannot tell, do not touch. Point and ask.

resources.title: Watch the four moves
resources.purpose: Shows the complete approved worked example.
content: A lamp cord stretches across the middle of a pictured walking path. The lamp is switched off.
1. Spot: I look from where I am standing. I see a cord crossing the path.
2. Stop: I do not step over it or touch the cord.
3. Name: I choose “trip” because a foot could catch on the cord.
4. Ask and check: I ask the guardian to handle it. After the adult moves it, I check that the walking path is clear.
The sample succeeds because the learner notices a specific condition, names how harm could happen, follows the no-touch rule, and leaves the physical fix to the guardian.

resources.title: Try the first move with a coach
resources.purpose: Carries the coached first attempt and fresh correction turn.
content: Picture card: An open cleaning bottle is sitting on a low table. You do not know what is inside.
What should you do first?
Pick it up so I can read it. — Stop. An unknown product is adult-only. Point without touching and ask the adult.
Point, say “poison or unsure,” and ask the adult. — That follows all three boundaries: point, name the possible risk, and ask.
Walk away without telling anyone. — Noticing is a good start. Add the ask step so the authorized adult knows what you saw.
Fresh coached card: A closed book is flat on a shelf and does not block a path. Say “safe in this picture” or “I am not sure,” then give one reason.
Move to independent work after the learner gives a reason and uses the point-without-touching boundary on the fresh card.

resources.title: Home Check — real-life path
resources.purpose: Delivers all five physical-route checkpoints and boundaries.
content: Stand at the guardian-chosen starting place. Do not open, move, or pick up anything.
Check the five checkpoints shown in the lesson: walking path, exit, heat area, products, and small objects.
At each checkpoint, say the risk word, say “safe in this check,” or say “I am not sure.” Give one reason.
Point out concerns. The guardian decides what counts and handles every physical item or change.
After the guardian is finished, look again from a safe place and say what condition changed. Do not record the room, item, or household details.
Checkpoint: Walking path
Checkpoint: Doorway or exit
Checkpoint: Heat or lamp area
Checkpoint: Cleaners, medicines, or unknown products
Checkpoint: Very small objects

Complete all five checks. Finding no hazard is a valid result when each check includes a risk-based reason. The guardian, not the learner or Tutor, certifies that the physical walkthrough and no-touch boundary occurred.

resources.title: Scene Check — equal-credit simulation
resources.purpose: Delivers all six equal-credit invented scenes.
content: For each complete scene, choose a risk word or “safe or unsure,” give one short reason, and state the safe next move. These are invented scenes; do not compare them with your home.
scene-1 — Hallway: A backpack strap lies across the walking path. The doorway is open.
scene-2 — Side table: An unlabeled spray bottle sits on a low table. No adult is in the picture.
scene-3 — Play area: Three tiny building pieces are on the floor beside a baby toy.
scene-4 — Reading corner: A paper decoration touches the shade of a lamp that is switched on.
scene-5 — Bookshelf: A closed book lies flat on a shelf. The walking path is clear.
scene-6 — Desk: A power cord has a split cover with wire showing. The learner stands several steps away.
Submit a response for all six scenes. A trusted human evaluates the risk reasoning; the browser and Tutor do not certify a physical event.

steps: 1. Spot: look from where you stand.
2. Stop: do not touch or step over the item.

guardianInvolvement.role: guardian gave permission and stayed present; learner used point-without-touching; guardian handled every physical change; all five checkpoints were considered
guardianInvolvement.signOffBoundary: The guardian certifies only the physical walkthrough. The guardian does not score the reflection or infer effort, honesty, maturity, responsibility, diagnosis, or character.

safety.stopRule: Stop, step back, do not touch, and tell the guardian whenever an item is unknown, sharp, hot, electrical, chemical, medicinal, broken, or hard to reach safely.
adultOnly: moving or opening any product or medicine
handling plugs, cords, electricity, heat, glass, or sharp items
deciding whether and how a physical condition should be changed
safety.unavailablePath: Use the embedded Scene Check. Lack of permission, adult time, a particular household space, or any planted hazard never lowers credit.
safety.noShameRule: Describe only the observable move and correction. Never label the learner, household, effort, maturity, responsibility, or character.

privacy.rule: Which move—spot, stop, name, or ask—helped you make a careful decision? Explain using an invented scene or only the risk word. Do not describe a private household item or room.

may: ask for a risk mechanism on invented scenes
mayNot: request private household details or media
observe or claim a physical condition
direct the learner to touch or move an item
tutorBoundary.physicalCompletionRule: Tutor may acknowledge saved learner evidence. Tutor cannot grant permission, observe the home, certify a physical walkthrough, or create guardian attestation.
tutorBoundary.missingResourceAction: Stop and identify the missing embedded item. Do not invent a replacement; route to the other fully delivered path only when its materials resolve.
